issue.description:
docs/ENHANCED-FEATURES.md (linked from README.md's Documentation section) contains an 'Implementation Checklist' claiming as done: '[x] Play/Pause animation controls' and '[x] Multiple speed options (1x, 30x, 60x, 2min)', plus a documented startAnimation() function at index.html:782-795 and workflow 'Time-Lapse Animation: Click Play button -> select speed -> watch sun traverse sky'.

This feature does NOT exist in the actual index.html (1207 lines). Verified via: grep -ni 'animat\|play\|pause\|speed' index.html — zero relevant matches (only an unrelated CSS 'animation: spin' keyframe for the loading spinner). The control-panel HTML (Location/Date/Timeline/Sun Info sections, index.html ~350-471) has no play/pause button or speed selector anywhere, and no requestAnimationFrame-driven time-lapse loop exists in the <script> block (confirmed function list: init, initMap, resizeSunPathCanvas, drawSunPath, drawLegend, initTimeline, updateTimeFromCanvas, drawTimeline, interpolateColor, initControls, changeDate, initDatePicker, reverseGeocode, updateLocation, updateSunInfo, updateHeaderTime, updateAll, formatTime — no startAnimation/animate/play/pause).

Implement the feature so the docs match reality:
1. Add a Play/Pause button and a speed selector (1x, 30x, 60x, 2min-per-frame, matching the doc's four presets) to the Timeline control-section in index.html.
2. Wire Play to a requestAnimationFrame loop that advances currentDate/time-of-day by the selected speed multiplier each frame and calls updateAll() (reuse existing update cascade — updateLocation/updateSunInfo/updateHeaderTime/drawTimeline/drawSunPath).
3. Pause must preserve the exact current time position (no drift/snap on resume).
4. Animation must wrap at midnight to the next day and keep looping until paused.
5. Playing must not conflict with the existing timeline mouse/touch drag-scrub interaction (dragging should pause or override playback cleanly, not fight it).
6. Manually verify in a browser (via serve.py): Play at 60x visibly moves the sun marker/timeline indicator through a full day in ~24 seconds; Pause stops it in place; switching speed while playing takes effect without restarting from 12 AM.

Acceptance criteria: feature works as described in docs/ENHANCED-FEATURES.md's 'Animation Controls' and 'Workflow 3: Time-Lapse Animation' sections; existing timeline scrubbing, date navigation, and keyboard shortcuts remain unaffected.
issue.title: Implement documented time-lapse animation controls (Play/Pause + speed presets)

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 §Decision (L79-89) — "Vendor Leaflet, SunCalc, and
Flatpickr (JS + CSS) into the repo under a new `vendor/` directory ... and served
same-origin from the Docker image alongside `index.html`."

## Observed (plan-vs-built sweep 2026-08-19)
index.html references five same-origin assets:
  /vendor/leaflet.css  /vendor/leaflet.js  /vendor/suncalc.min.js
  /vendor/flatpickr.min.js  /vendor/flatpickr.min.css
`git ls-files vendor/` returns only leaflet.css and leaflet.js. The other three
were never vendored, so three of the page's five assets have no source file at all.

Introduced by 187be4f "chore(lab): preserve local work before removing duplicate
clone", which shipped the index.html rewrite with only part of the vendoring.

One bead rather than three: the three files land in one directory in one commit,
and splitting invites three concurrent workers into the same path.

Pin versions per ADR-001: suncalc@1.9.0; flatpickr at the latest stable at the time
of vendoring, recorded in the commit message.

## Done when
    git ls-files vendor/ | sort
-> lists exactly:
    vendor/flatpickr.min.css
    vendor/flatpickr.min.js
    vendor/leaflet.css
    vendor/leaflet.js
    vendor/suncalc.min.js

and every path referenced by index.html resolves to a tracked file:

    for f in $(grep -oE '/vendor/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' index.html | sort -u); do
      git ls-files --error-unmatch ".${f}" >/dev/null || echo "MISSING $f"
    done
-> prints nothing
issue.title: Vendor the suncalc and flatpickr assets that vendor/ is missing

issue.description:
serve.py's run_server() contains a directory-resolution fallback that references a different, unrelated repo:

    if os.path.exists('/app/index.html'):
        os.chdir('/app')
    elif os.path.exists('/workspaces/ord-options-testing/sun-simulator'):
        os.chdir('/workspaces/ord-options-testing/sun-simulator')
    # else: stay in current directory

'/workspaces/ord-options-testing/sun-simulator' is a leftover/copy-pasted path from an unrelated devcontainer project (ord-options-testing) and has nothing to do with sun-sim. It is misleading (a future maintainer could reasonably assume this path is meaningful to this repo) and is dead code in every real deployment path: Docker always has /app/index.html so it never falls through, and every other run mode (python3 serve.py from repo root, docker-compose, any generic HTTP server per the README's 'Option 4') already works by staying in the current directory per the existing '# else' comment.

Fix: remove the incorrect elif branch entirely (the existing '/app' check plus 'stay in current directory' fallback already covers every documented run mode in README.md's Quick Start section). Optionally replace with a generic fallback anchored to the script's own directory (os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) if extra robustness is desired, but a plain removal is sufficient and matches current documented usage.

Acceptance criteria: the unrelated hardcoded path is gone from serve.py; 'python3 serve.py' still serves index.html correctly when run from the repo root and via 'docker build/run' per the README's Quick Start instructions.
issue.title: Remove stale hardcoded fallback path in serve.py referencing unrelated 'ord-options-testing' project

issue.description:
docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20) decided to vendor the three CDN-loaded JS/CSS deps (Leaflet 1.9.4, SunCalc 1.9.0, Flatpickr) into a new vendor/ directory, served same-origin, instead of loading them from unpkg.com/cdn.jsdelivr.net at runtime. The ADR explicitly states follow-up work would be tracked as a bead referencing it (label artifact-improvement) — no such bead was ever created; verified via bf list --json, no bead in this workspace references vendoring, ADR-001, or a vendor/ directory, and index.html still loads all three libs directly from CDN (grep unpkg.com/jsdelivr.net index.html: lines 9, 14, 564, 567, 568 unchanged).

Concrete problems this leaves live in production (sunsim.jedarden.com):
1. Flatpickr is loaded unpinned (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/flatpickr with no version segment) with no Subresource Integrity hash, unlike the Leaflet tags which do have SRI.
2. Availability is coupled to two third-party CDNs; an unpkg.com or jsdelivr.net outage makes the app unusable even though sunsim.jedarden.com itself is healthy, and k8s liveness/readiness probes (GET / only) would not detect this failure mode.
3. serve.py sends Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate on every response (confirmed at serve.py:20) with no local static assets to cache, so there is no browser caching story at all currently.

Implement per ADR-001 Decision section:
1. Create vendor/ directory, fetch/commit leaflet@1.9.4 (css+js), suncalc@1.9.0 (js), and flatpickr (css+js, pin to latest stable at implementation time) — combined size should stay under ~300KB uncompressed per the ADR.
2. Update index.html to reference /vendor/... paths instead of the CDN URLs at lines 9, 14, 564, 567, 568.
3. Update serve.py to send a long-lived immutable Cache-Control header (e.g. public, max-age=31536000, immutable) for anything under /vendor/, while keeping index.html itself on the existing no-cache policy.

Acceptance criteria: app loads and functions identically with network access to unpkg.com/cdn.jsdelivr.net blocked (only same-origin requests); vendor/ files are committed at pinned versions; serve.py serves long-lived cache headers for /vendor/ paths only.
issue.title: Vendor Leaflet/SunCalc/Flatpickr into repo per ADR-001 (never implemented)

Along the way fixed two adjacent defects the verification exposed: serve.py poisoning CDNs with immutable-cached 404s (a80c380) and unversioned asset URLs (b59e052, ?v=1). Shipped as 0.1.8 (356096f), rolled via the normal sensor->kaniko->declarative-config->ArgoCD pipeline. Full findings and the observed pipeline race documented in bead notes.
issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 §Decision (L83-84) — the vendored files are
"served same-origin from the Docker image alongside `index.html`".

## Observed (plan-vs-built sweep 2026-08-19)
Dockerfile copies only:
    COPY index.html .
    COPY serve.py .
    COPY docs/ ./docs/
`vendor/` is never copied, so even the two files that ARE vendored (leaflet.css,
leaflet.js) are absent from the built image.

This is the live break. On https://sunsim.jedarden.com today:
    200  /                          (index.html, references /vendor/*)
    404  /vendor/leaflet.js
    404  /vendor/suncalc.min.js
    404  /vendor/flatpickr.min.js
Leaflet (map), SunCalc (all solar math) and Flatpickr (date picker) therefore fail
to load. The k8s probes only GET / , which returns 200, so the outage is invisible
to the cluster -- the failure mode ADR-001 §Context item 3 predicted.

## Done when
    grep -n 'COPY vendor' Dockerfile
-> prints a COPY line for vendor/

and the built image actually contains them:

    docker build -t sunsim-verify . \
      && docker run --rm sunsim-verify ls /app/vendor
-> lists all five vendored files
issue.notes:
Fix shipped and verified live, but the vendor COPY turned out to be only the first layer of the outage — two follow-on defects found and fixed in the same chain:

1. Dockerfile now COPYs vendor/ (ea40c7e). Image verified locally (docker build + ls /app/vendor, all five files) and in-registry.

2. serve.py stamped max-age=31536000, immutable on EVERY /vendor/ response including 404s. While vendor/ was missing, Cloudflare cached the 404s at the edge with a year TTL (observed: cf-cache-status HIT, age 45203 on /vendor/leaflet.js) — so the site stayed broken AFTER the image was fixed. Fixed status-aware headers in a80c380; live 404s now return no-cache.

3. index.html asset references bumped to ?v=1 (b59e052) — fresh CDN cache keys, immediately unblocked users without needing a Cloudflare purge (no accessible token has zone cache-purge scope: Pages token is zone-blind; external-dns token is DNS-scoped; its kubeconfig path in CLAUDE.md is also stale — ardenone-manager.kubeconfig does not exist, only ardenone-manager-temp.kubeconfig pointing at a dead localhost:16443 tunnel).

Pipeline defect observed (pre-existing, NOT fixed here — needs its own bead): sensor-triggered builds race the Forgejo->GitHub mirror and each other. Three concurrent runs (nbd8h/l6nvd/txzgg) all resolved version 0.1.7 and pushed overlapping/rewritten auto-bump commits (d0a5a77 vanished from main history; ghcr tag 0.1.7 was built from different commits by different runs). issue.description:
OPS-GATED: needs credential/infra work (Forgejo repo + push-mirror setup, GitHub Actions repo-settings changes) and a human call on cutover timing given in-flight CI migration.

Workspace policy (CLAUDE.md Git Hosting section) requires every repo to be hosted on Forgejo (git.ardenone.com) as source of truth, with GitHub as a read-only server-side push mirror. Verified this repo does NOT follow that pattern: git remote -v in the sun-sim checkout shows origin = https://github.com/jedarden/sun-sim.git for BOTH fetch and push — there is no Forgejo remote at all. This looks like pre-policy legacy setup (initial commit dated 2025-11-14).

Compounding this, .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml is still present AND actively enabled — confirmed by git log showing real recent auto-bump commits pushed by the workflow itself (9d6ed5e "ci: auto-bump version to 0.1.4", f5753cc "ci: auto-bump version to 0.1.5") interleaved with the NEW Argo Events webhook trigger that was wired in the same window (commit bc8df73, 2026-07-22, per bf-11s/bf-p9k/bf-3gw notes) and which itself already triggered a live sun-sim-build Argo workflow on 2026-07-28 (per notes/bf-p9k.md). Two independent, un-coordinated CI systems are therefore both watching pushes to the same github.com/jedarden/sun-sim.git origin right now:
- The GH Actions workflow auto-bumps VERSION on any push touching index.html/serve.py/Dockerfile/docs/, with no filter on commit-message prefix (only a file-diff check) — so it would re-trigger on the Argo pipeline's own "ci: auto-bump version to X" commits (that message does not contain [skip ci]).
- The Argo sensor (sun-sim-sensor.yml) cascade-guards on head_commit.message not matching "^ci: auto-bump" — but the GH Actions workflow's own bump-commit message is "chore: bump version to X [skip ci]" (github.com/jedarden/sun-sim .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml, step "Commit version bump"), which does NOT match that filter pattern, so it would also re-trigger a NEW Argo build.
- The GH Actions workflow also still pushes a "latest" tag to ghcr.io (docker/metadata-action step, type=raw,value=latest,enable=true) — a banned pattern per workspace policy (never use :latest image tags).

Currently observed live symptom: VERSION file in git is 0.1.5, but the actual running pod in ardenone-cluster/utilities (kubectl get deployment sun-sim -n utilities) is still on ghcr.io/jedarden/sun-sim:0.1.4 — the two pipelines have already drifted out of sync with each other and with the deployed manifest.

Note: bf-2bc (verify Argo CI green end-to-end) and bf-4ke (remove .github/workflows after Argo verified) already track the planned clean shutdown of GH Actions — this bead does NOT duplicate that removal work. This bead covers the two things neither of those track: (a) migrating the repo's git origin itself to the Forgejo-primary + GitHub-push-mirror pattern per CLAUDE.md Git Hosting section, and (b) flagging that the dual-CI cascade risk described above is live NOW, not just a future risk once Argo is verified — a human should judge whether to accelerate bf-4ke or temporarily disable the GH Actions workflow via repo settings (not just deleting the file, per hub-git reference_gh_actions_repo_level_drift) while the migration is still in progress, rather than waiting for the full sequential gate.

Acceptance criteria: sun-sim hosted on git.ardenone.com as origin with GitHub as an automated read-only push mirror (per CLAUDE.md steps); GitHub Actions disabled at the repo-settings level (not just workflow-file deletion); confirm no further concurrent GH-Actions-vs-Argo builds after cutover.
issue.title: OPS-GATED: sun-sim git origin is GitHub-direct, not Forgejo-primary; GitHub Actions still live in parallel with new Argo CI trigger

issue.description:
Several confirmed inaccuracies between README.md/docs/*.md and actual shipped index.html:

1. README.md:265 footer hardcodes "Version: 0.1.0" but VERSION file (repo root) is at 0.1.5 and has been bumped multiple times by CI — footer never updated since initial commit.
2. README.md Performance Metrics table claims "Bundle Size: 87KB (gzipped)" — actual measured size is gzip -9 index.html = 11409 bytes (~11KB), roughly 8x smaller than claimed. Also two DIFFERENT accuracy numbers are asserted for the same thing in the same file: Features section says "±0.01 degrees position, ±1 minute timing" while Performance Metrics table says "±0.0067 degrees / ±39 seconds" for what should be the same SunCalc-derived figure.
3. Three commits (5ebc2a2 feat: add GitHub repository link to header, c14c6ac feat: add GPS location button with geolocation API, 071afe9 feat: add automatic city name detection with reverse geocoding) shipped real user-facing features that are NOT listed anywhere in README.md Features section or in any docs/*.md file. Verified present in index.html: gps-btn/btn-use-gps (lines ~460-466), navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition (line 1147), Nominatim reverse-geocoding call (lines 1288-1320).
4. docs/COMPASS-ROSE-FEATURE.md, docs/DATE-NAVIGATION.md, and docs/ENHANCED-FEATURES.md each cite specific index.html line ranges for key functions (e.g. "Main Function: drawSunPath() (index.html:505-680)" in COMPASS-ROSE-FEATURE.md, "index.html:597-650" in ENHANCED-FEATURES.md) that are now stale — index.html has grown from the original 1207 lines to 1408 lines (GPS/geocoding features plus the time-lapse animation controls added since), and drawSunPath() is now actually at line 633, not 505 or 597.

Fix: update README.md footer/version badge to read from or match VERSION file (or state versioning is automatic and drop the hardcoded number), reconcile the two conflicting accuracy figures to one sourced number, add GPS-location/auto-city-detection/GitHub-link entries to the Features list, and refresh the stale line-number references in the three docs/*.md feature docs to match current index.html.

Acceptance criteria: no hardcoded version number in README.md that contradicts VERSION file; one consistent accuracy claim; all three newer features listed in README Features; line references in docs/*.md verified against current index.html.

issue.description:
The repo has NO test files whatsoever — verified via 'find . -iname *test* -not -path ./.git/*' returning empty, and no tests/ directory, package.json, or CI test step exists anywhere in the repo. Yet README.md explicitly advertises numeric accuracy claims under 'Performance Metrics': Position Accuracy ±0.0067°, Timing Accuracy ±39 seconds, and under Features: 'High Accuracy - ±0.01° position, ±1 minute timing'. None of this is verified by any automated check — a regression in the sun-position/time math (e.g. from a future edit to updateSunInfo(), drawSunPath(), or the SunCalc integration) would ship silently. docs/architecture.md (Status: Draft) section 7 'Testing Strategy' also documents an intended test approach with concrete reference cases (equator ~12h day length, arctic circle midnight sun/polar night, mid-latitude seasonal variation) that was never implemented.

Scope (deliberately minimal — do not attempt the full Vitest/Testing-Library/E2E pyramid described in architecture.md, that is out of scope):
1. Add a single automated test file (e.g. using Playwright, already a reasonable fit since the app is a static page served by serve.py) that: starts serve.py (or a static server) headless, loads index.html, and for a small fixed set of known lat/lon/date inputs asserts the displayed values in #info-azimuth, #info-altitude, #info-sunrise, #info-sunset, #info-daylength match expected reference values within a small tolerance (e.g. +/-2 minutes for times, +/-0.5 degrees for azimuth/altitude — do not over-tighten past what SunCalc itself guarantees).
2. Include at minimum these reference cases: (a) a location near the equator on an equinox date, expecting day length close to 12h; (b) a known city/date/time with independently-verifiable sunrise/sunset (e.g. from timeanddate.com or NOAA) to sanity-check the geocoding-independent math; (c) a point above the Arctic Circle on the summer solstice, expecting the day-length field to read '24h (Midnight Sun)' (exercises the existing polar-handling branch in updateSunInfo()).
3. Add a package.json (currently absent) with a 'test' script that runs this, and a short usage note in docs/ (e.g. docs/notes/testing.md) on how to run it locally and what it covers.

Acceptance criteria: 'npm test' (or documented equivalent) runs the new test(s) against a locally served instance and passes; test file is committed; no changes made to index.html's actual calculation logic (this bead is test-only, not a fix).
